cf.title: [PATCH v1] Fix for Bug#19724 - ALTER TYPE ... ALTER ATTRIBUTE triggers internal error for base type of domain with check

input.subject: [PATCH v1] Fix for Bug#19724 - ALTER TYPE ... ALTER ATTRIBUTE triggers internal error for base type of domain with check

verdict_reasoning: The goal is a bug fix for an internal error and a possible crash on every supported branch, and reviewers agree on 0001. Two fixable design points remain for stable branches: replication-ondisk-2 (0003 widens the name-based domain lookup race to domains the caller does not own) and standards-compat-1 (0002 touches an exported prototype in typecmds.h). Neither blocks the idea, but a committer must decide what goes to back branches.

brief.title: Fix ALTER ... TYPE error when a domain check depends on the type
brief.problem: ALTER TYPE ... ALTER ATTRIBUTE ... TYPE and ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE fail with "could not identify relation associated with constraint" when a domain over a non-composite type (int, float8, int[], a domain over a domain) has a CHECK that references the altered composite type or row type. The bug dates from af20e2d72 (v11), so every supported branch has it.
brief.proposed_design: 0001 attaches the domain constraint rebuild to the relation being altered (tab->relid) instead of deriving a relation from the domain's base type. 0002 re-adds the domain constraint without validation and validates it after phase 3 rewrites, so rows are no longer read with the new tuple descriptor over the old heap. 0003 skips ownership checks when rebuilding constraints and restores comments with CreateComments() instead of CommentObject().
user_visible_surface: ALTER TYPE ... ALTER ATTRIBUTE ... TYPE and ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE succeed where they failed with an internal error.
The rebuild no longer takes AccessExclusiveLock on another composite type's relation when the domain is over that other type.
Altering your own type no longer fails with "must be owner of type/relation" because of another user's dependent domain or commented constraint.
Domain constraint validation errors now come after table rewrites, not during phase 2.
AlterDomainAddConstraint() changes in typecmds.h, a C API visible to extensions.
author_claims: Using tab->relid is safe because the relid only picks which relation gets locked and which work queue entry gets the command.
The fix, with tests, applies cleanly to REL_14_STABLE through REL_19_STABLE; reviewers support back-patching.
Early validation can give wrong values, false constraint violations, "type with OID 4294967295 does not exist", or a crash.
Ownership checks make no sense on re-add because the matching drop is done without permission checks.
Any user can block a type owner's ALTER, since types grant USAGE to PUBLIC by default.
brief.thread_state: Ayush Tiwari, Rahul Yadav, Matheus Alcantara and Zsolt Parragi reviewed; Matheus wrote 0002 and 0003, and v4 is the latest. Open points: whether to squash 0001 and 0002, Ayush's pending review of 0003, and the name-based domain lookup race, which the author suggests fixing later without back-patching.
unclear: Whether 0002 and 0003 are meant for back-patching to all branches, or only 0001.
Whether skipping ownership checks in 0003 is acceptable as a security behaviour change in stable branches; no committer has commented.
Whether a domain renamed and replaced concurrently can still receive the constraint silently under v4.
Whether the ROW(VALUE, NULL)::t recursion seen in testing (stack depth exceeded) will be handled anywhere.
Whether the new validation loop needs CommandCounterIncrement() between constraints; Ayush and Matheus disagree.

objections.title: Name-based re-add can attach a constraint to the wrong domain
objections.failure_scenario: Session A runs ALTER TYPE while session B renames domain d and creates a new domain d over the same type. The rebuilt d_check is stored in pg_constraint on the new domain, and the original domain loses it. Later inserts into columns of the original domain skip the check, and pg_dump keeps the wrong state.
objections.argument: Message #10 shows this race succeeding silently, and message #11 defers the fix to a separate patch that would not be back-patched. The bug is older than this patch, but 0003 removes the ownership check, so after v4 the stale lookup also succeeds when the domain belongs to another user. 0002 already tracks constraint OIDs in the work queue, so resolving the domain by OID may not need much more code.
objections.author_must_show: Can the re-add use the domain OID taken before the drop, so that 0003 does not ship to stable branches while the name lookup can still pick the wrong domain?

critic.reasoning: Message #10 confirms the constraint can silently move to a new domain of the same name, and that 0003 extends this to domains the caller does not own. Message #11 defers the fix without back-patching, so the concern is open for stable branches.

objections.title: 0002 changes an exported function signature in a back-patched fix
objections.failure_scenario: An extension built against an earlier minor release of 14 through 19 calls AlterDomainAddConstraint(). After a minor upgrade, the server passes or expects arguments the extension's compiled call does not supply. The extension then fails at load time, or misbehaves at run time.
objections.argument: 0002 touches src/include/commands/typecmds.h and changes AlterDomainAddConstraint(), so the fix depends on a changed prototype. Message #3 supports back-patching to REL_14_STABLE through REL_19_STABLE, and the CommitFest entry targets stable. The thread checks only that v1 applies cleanly. Nobody has said whether 0002 goes to the back branches, or how its signature change would be kept ABI-compatible there.
objections.author_must_show: For back branches, will 0002 keep the existing AlterDomainAddConstraint() signature, for example with a new wrapper function, so extensions built against earlier minor releases keep working?

critic.reasoning: The thread does not say whether 0002 goes to back branches or how the typecmds.h change stays ABI-compatible there. The material shows only that the header is touched, so the author should confirm whether an existing signature changes or a declaration is only added.

refuted.title: Back-patched AlterDomainAddConstraint() signature change breaks extension ABI
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension built against 17.x calls AlterDomainAddConstraint() with the old argument list. After a minor update that includes 0002, the server calls the function with a different signature. The extension misbehaves or crashes, and nobody finds out before the upgrade.
refuted.argument: 0002 changes src/include/commands/typecmds.h, and the brief lists AlterDomainAddConstraint() as a C API visible to extensions. Message #3 supports back-patching to REL_14_STABLE through REL_19_STABLE, and the thread does not say whether 0002 and 0003 go to back branches. Stable branches usually keep exported signatures fixed, for example through a new function or a wrapper. The patch prose does not say how the back-branch versions handle this.
refuted.author_must_show: For the back branches, will 0002 keep the existing AlterDomainAddConstraint() signature and add a separate entry point for the skip-validation case?

refuted.title: 0003 runs another user's domain check code as the ALTER caller
refuted.failure_scenario: Bob, unprivileged, creates a domain whose CHECK calls his own plpgsql function and references a superuser-owned type. The superuser runs ALTER TYPE ... ALTER ATTRIBUTE, and 0002/0003 re-add and validate Bob's constraint, executing his function as superuser. Today the same ALTER stops at checkDomainOwner() before any of Bob's code runs.
refuted.argument: 0003 removes the ownership check because the drop has none and table CHECK rebuilds have none (message #5). Removing it also removes the only barrier that kept the type owner from running a dependent domain's check expression, and 0002 always validates that expression after the rewrites. Maintenance paths that run untrusted owners' code switch to the object owner under a restricted security context. The proposal does not say whose identity runs the deferred validateDomainCheckConstraint() call.
refuted.author_must_show: Does the deferred validation in 0002 run as the domain owner under SECURITY_RESTRICTED_OPERATION, and if not, why is running it as the ALTER caller acceptable in stable branches?

critic.reasoning: Message #5 notes that rebuilding another user's table CHECK constraint already has no ownership check, and that rebuild revalidates the expression as the ALTER caller. Bob can reach the same result today with a table CHECK, so 0003 follows existing practice and adds no new exposure.

refuted.title: Without the ownership check, the name lookup race can modify other users' domains
refuted.failure_scenario: During a long ALTER TYPE, the original domain d is renamed and a different user creates a new domain d in the same schema. The rebuilt constraint lands on the new user's domain without that user's consent and without any permission check. Nobody notices until inserts into that user's columns start failing.
refuted.argument: Message #10 shows the re-add resolves the domain by name, and that 0003 lets this succeed when the domain belongs to someone other than the user running the ALTER. Message #11 proposes fixing the lookup later and without back-patching. Back-patching 0003 alone ships the wider exposure to all branches and leaves out the fix. Capturing the domain OID before the drop would remove the problem.
refuted.author_must_show: Can 0003 be back-patched only together with an OID-based domain lookup, or held back until that lookup exists?

refuted.title: Back-patching 0002 changes an exported function signature in stable branches
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension built against 17.x calls AlterDomainAddConstraint() with the old argument list. The user installs a minor release that carries 0002 and does not rebuild the extension. The call passes the wrong arguments, and the result is a crash or wrong behaviour that shows up only at run time.
refuted.argument: 0002 touches src/include/commands/typecmds.h and changes AlterDomainAddConstraint(). Message #3 proposes back-patching to REL_14_STABLE, and the brief says the fix applies through REL_19_STABLE. The thread does not say whether 0002 goes back too, or how the stable-branch ABI is kept. Stable branches usually keep the old symbol and add a new function or a wrapper.
refuted.author_must_show: For the back branches, does 0002 keep the existing AlterDomainAddConstraint() signature, for example through a new function, so that extensions built against older minor releases still work?

refuted.title: Back-patching 0003 widens a known race whose fix is planned for master only
refuted.failure_scenario: On a stable branch with 0003 applied, a concurrent session renames another user's domain and creates a new domain with the old name during ALTER TYPE. The rebuilt constraint lands on the wrong domain without an error, and the owner of that domain is not checked. Nobody notices until values that should have been rejected appear.
refuted.argument: Message #10 shows that the re-add finds the domain by name, so the constraint can move to a different domain. It also says that 0003 makes this work against domains owned by other users. Message #11 proposes fixing the lookup later, without back-patching. Stable branches would then carry the wider exposure with no planned fix, and no committer has commented on that trade-off.
refuted.author_must_show: Will 0003 go to stable branches before the domain is re-added by OID, and if so, why is the wider window from the name-based lookup acceptable there?

touch_points.reason: The rebuild drops and re-creates pg_constraint rows for domain CHECK constraints, and finds the domain by name.

touch_points.label: security / privileges

touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets stable, and 0002 and 0003 change a C prototype and permission behaviour.

questions: Which of 0001, 0002 and 0003 are meant for back-patching to REL_14_STABLE through REL_19_STABLE?
Can the re-add use the domain OID taken before the drop, so 0003 does not reach stable branches while the name lookup can pick another user's domain?
For back branches, does 0002 keep the existing AlterDomainAddConstraint() signature, for example through a new wrapper function?
Does the new validation loop after phase 3 need CommandCounterIncrement() between constraints, and what case shows it?
Will the stack depth error seen with a ROW(VALUE, NULL)::t check be handled in this patch set or left as is?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the ALTER TABLE phase 2 and phase 3 work queue in tablecmds.c and the domain constraint code in typecmds.c; no such committer has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a back-patched change to ALTER TABLE rewrite ordering, a relaxed ownership check, and an exported prototype, on six branches for their remaining support life.
committability.author_follow_up: The author and a co-author posted revisions up to v4 within about six weeks and answered review comments, which suggests they stay for fixes.

priority.reason: The bug gives an internal error or a crash on all supported branches, but only for domains whose CHECK references an altered composite or row type. The three patches are small, yet back-patching 0002 and 0003 needs a committer's decision and none is engaged.

provisional_note: Without the code, I could not check whether 0002 changes the existing AlterDomainAddConstraint() signature or only adds a declaration. I also could not check how the deferred validation orders its catalog updates or which identity it runs under.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Laurenz Albe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX to replace the index behind an EXCLUDE, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY constraint with a similar index. The main use case is swapping a primary key index for one with INCLUDE columns, or back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane wanted the feature rejected because a primary key with a swapped index is no longer an accurate primary key, and information_schema cannot describe it. The author did not answer the review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add support for ON UPDATE/DELETE actions on ALTER CONSTRAINT
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends alter table ... alter constraint so it can change the ON UPDATE and ON DELETE actions of a foreign key. It also changes alter constraint to keep the deferrability options the user did not name, and later added an alter constraint ... set variant that changes only the named properties.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the same deferrability syntax should not mean different things depending on the constraint's previous state, and suggested full replacement or a new add or replace constraint command. Wolfgang Walther objected that the SET variant had the same implied-change problem and proposed separate per-action foreign key syntax. The thread reached no agreement on the syntax, and David Steele returned the patch because it had not been updated for over a year and no longer applied.

precedents_retrieved.title: Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
Reverted commit(s): Revert to 9.6 treatment of ALTER TYPE enumtype ADD VALUE.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Originally committed as 15bc038f (plus some follow-ups), this was
reverted in 28e07270 due to a problem discovered in parallel
workers.  This new version corrects that problem by sending the
list of uncommitted enum values to parallel workers.

Here follows the original commit message describing the change:

To prevent possibly breaking indexes on enum columns, we must keep
uncommitted enum values from getting stored in tables, unless we
can be sure that any such column is new in the current transaction.

Formerly, we enforced this by disallowing ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE
from being executed at all in a transaction block, unless the target
enum type had been created in the current transaction.  This patch
removes that restriction, and instead insists that an uncommitted enum
value can't be referenced unless it belongs to an enum type created
in the same transaction as the value.  Per discussion, this should be
a bit less onerous.  It does require each function that could possibly
return a new enum value to SQL operations to check this restriction,
but there aren't so many of those that this seems unmaintainable.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
Reverted commit(s): Add regression test for bug fixed by recent refactoring.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
A view defined as "select <something> where false" had the curious property
that the system wouldn't check whether users had the privileges necessary
to select from it.  More generally, permissions checks could be skipped
for tables referenced in sub-selects or views that were proven empty by
constraint exclusion (although some quick testing suggests this seldom
happens in cases of practical interest).  This happened because the planner
failed to include rangetable entries for such tables in the finished plan.

This was noticed in connection with erroneous handling of materialized
views, but actually the issue is quite unrelated to matviews.  Therefore,
revert commit 200ba1667b3a8d7a9d559d2f05f83d209c9d8267 in favor of a more
direct test for the real problem.

Back-patch to 9.2 where the bug was introduced (by commit
7741dd6590073719688891898e85f0cb73453159).

precedents_retrieved.title: CREATEROLE and role ownership hierarchies
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set reduces what the CREATEROLE attribute allows and adds role ownership, so each role has an owner and non-superuser creators manage only the subtree of roles they own. After upgrade, the bootstrap superuser owns all existing roles, and REASSIGN OWNED and ALTER ROLE OWNER TO move ownership.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers did not agree on role ownership as the model. They objected that an owner would bypass most privilege checks on the roles it owns, and preferred building on SQL-standard ADMIN OPTION with separate grants that a superuser can revoke from creators. With no agreement and v15 too close, only the removal of the session-user self-administration exception was committed. Robert Haas proposed returning the entry, since later work might not take this form.

Stephen's, and now my, issue with ownership is that, since it implies

precedents_retrieved.title: Reduce lock level for ALTER TABLE ... ADD CHECK
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lowers the lock level for ALTER TABLE ... ADD CHECK to ShareRowExclusiveLock, matching what was already done for foreign key constraints. The author argued this is safe because check constraints do not affect running SELECTs until validated; a second patch extended lock reductions to other ALTER TABLE forms.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane showed that ADD CHECK updates both pg_class.relchecks and pg_constraint, so with the lower lock a concurrent session can read a relchecks count that does not match pg_constraint and fail in CheckConstraintFetch. He demonstrated this with a debugger. Replacing relchecks with a boolean could fix it, but he doubted the gain was worth the compatibility cost, and the author agreed to return the patch.

requires a considerable rewrite, which may or may not be possible to
accomplish in time for beta2.  In my judgment reviewing the rewrite will
be easier to accomplish starting from a clean slate, so let's temporarily
revert what's there now.  This also leaves us in a safe state if it turns
out to be necessary to postpone the rewrite to the next development cycle.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the search returned no earlier rejected, returned or withdrawn proposal of the same or a similar idea. Message #1 points to the 2017 thread behind af20e2d72, which showed the same float8 case without a test; that is the origin of the bug, not a rejected attempt at this fix.

Beyond the ABI point, this is a bug fix with no new syntax, GUC, catalog object or pg_dump surface. The later error timing in 0002 and the relaxed ownership checks in 0003 move behaviour toward what users would expect, and I found no concrete compatibility failure in either.

There is no on-disk format, WAL, replication, wire protocol or catalog schema change. The only issues on this angle are the exported C API in typecmds.h and how persistent constraint rows are re-attached.
0001 and 0002 raise no privilege concern on their own. Both objections concern 0003, mainly in combination with back-patching.
The core fix, 0001, has no maintenance or fit objection from this angle. It is a narrow bug fix in existing code, has no hot-path cost, and several reviewers agree on it.

This is a bug fix for an internal error in ALTER ... TYPE, and no existing feature, option or extension avoids it. The only workaround is to drop the domain constraint, alter the type and re-add the constraint by hand. That is a workaround for a bug and not an alternative design, so this angle has nothing to raise.

This is a bug fix, so the demand test does not apply. The command fails with an internal XX000 error or crashes, it was reported as bug #19724, and four reviewers reproduced it on every supported branch. Rarity of the setup (message #1) is no reason to keep an internal error or a crash. Whether 0003's ownership change belongs in stable branches is a design question for other angles.
